subsystems.name: Sensor filament
subsystems.role: the tiny wire under the skin that reacts with glucose in interstitial fluid.

subsystems.name: Transmitter electronics
subsystems.role: converts the electrochemical current into a digital reading and sends it by radio.

subsystems.name: Patch and applicator
subsystems.role: holds the device on the skin and inserts the filament with minimal pain.

subsystems.name: Algorithm and app
subsystems.role: turns raw sensor current into a glucose value, compensates for lag and shows trends.

buildSteps.title: Make the enzyme electrode
buildSteps.detail: A platinum or gold wire is coated with glucose oxidase, the enzyme that oxidises glucose and produces a small electric current.

buildSteps.title: Add protective membranes
buildSteps.detail: Layers of polymer are applied to keep out proteins and cells, limit oxygen interference and extend the sensor's working life.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The filament is bonded to a miniature potentiostat, microcontroller, Bluetooth chip and button cell inside a plastic housing.

buildSteps.title: Build the applicator
buildSteps.detail: A spring-loaded needle and the sensor are loaded into a sterile single-use inserter that pushes the filament just under the skin.

buildSteps.title: Sterilise and package
buildSteps.detail: The patch and applicator are sealed and sterilised so the filament can be placed safely.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate in batches
buildSteps.detail: Production units are tested against known glucose solutions; modern devices are factory-calibrated so users need no finger pricks.

buildSteps.title: Apply and pair
buildSteps.detail: The user presses the applicator onto the arm or abdomen, then pairs the transmitter with a phone app that receives readings every few minutes.

prerequisites.why: it is the core chemistry that turns glucose into a measurable current.
the filament must sit in tissue for days or weeks without causing rejection or drift.
a coin-cell battery must run the radio and sensor for the whole wear period.
interstitial glucose lags blood glucose, so software must correct the delay and filter noise.

pathway.milestone: 7–14 day wearable sensors that replace most finger-stick tests
pathway.unlocks: real-time glucose visibility and better day-to-day diabetes management.

pathway.milestone: sensors linked to insulin pumps for hybrid closed-loop delivery
pathway.unlocks: automatic adjustments of insulin between meals, already partly available.

pathway.milestone: longer wear times and multi-analyte sensing
pathway.unlocks: fewer replacements and monitoring of ketones or lactate alongside glucose.

pathway.milestone: fully implantable sensors lasting a year or more
pathway.unlocks: set-and-forget monitoring, including for people without diabetes who want metabolic insight.
